**ADMISSION DIAGNOSIS**: No admission diagnoses are documented for this encounter.
**SUBJECTIVE**
Anthony Dimarcello is a right handed 41 y.o. male with chronic ongoing medical problems (PMH) of none brought in by self for evaluation and treatment of left shoulder pain. Ortho was consulted for left comminuted humeral head/neck fracture with posterior dislocation of the humeral head. DOI: 08/29/2024. Patient states that on date of injury he was skateboarding down a hill when he slipped over some soapy pavement and landed directly onto the left shoulder in an attempt to roll into the fall. Patient states that he was seen at Hoag Newport beach and was placed in a sling and told it was a nonoperative injury. However patient wanted a second opinion and was recommended to Arrowhead Regional Medical Center. He reports persistent swelling to left upper extremity from shoulder to elbow with pain. Has not been able to range the shoulder or elbow normally since date of injury. Reports occasional tingling and numbness in certain positions. Patient is originally from Huntington Beach.
No L shoulder imaging when originally consulted. L shoulder XR taken at 1613. L shoulder CT taken at 1842.

item.caption: CT SHOULDER LEFT WO IV CONTRAST - Final result (09/02/2024 6:19 PM PDT)

paragraph.content: Displaced comminuted left humeral head and neck fracture with posterior dislocation of the humeral head fragment.
LEFT SHOULDER CT WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:
INDICATION: Status post trauma with pain.
COMPARISON: None.
TECHNIQUE: Axial images, along with reconstructed coronal and sagittal images were obtained through the left shoulder without intravenous contrast.
CT Dose Report (DLP) = 1009 mGy*cm.
CTDIvol = 38 mGy.

All CT is performed utilizing one of the following dose lowering techniques: automated exposure control, adjustment of the mA and/or kV according to patient size, and the use of iterative reconstruction technique.

FINDINGS: The alignment is satisfactory at the acromioclavicular joint. There is moderately displaced comminuted right humeral head and neck fracture with posterior dislocation of the left humeral head fragment with respect to glenoid. There is superior subluxation of the left humeral head. The scapula and clavicle are intact.
